templates.name: Caps Lock: Escape and Control
templates.why: Caps Lock is a big key in a great spot that almost nobody needs. Now a quick tap is Escape, and holding it is Control, so shortcuts like Control+C are easy to reach.
templates.forWho: Anyone who uses Terminal, a code editor, or Vim, and anyone who hits Caps Lock by accident.
changes: Hold Caps Lock and press another key: Control
Caps Lock no longer shouts in capital letters
templates.caution: Hold it a moment longer to get Control. If you type very fast right before it, it may give Escape instead.

rules.description: Caps Lock: tap is Escape, hold is Control

templates.name: Home row starter: Shift and Command
templates.why: Your fingers rest on A S D F and J K L ;. Hold F or J to get Shift, hold D or K to get Command, without moving your hand. Just four keys, so it is a gentle way to try the idea.
templates.forWho: First-timers who want to try home-row keys before using all eight.
changes: Tapping the same keys types the letter as usual
A key only turns into a modifier when you press a key from the other hand
templates.caution: Give it a week. Most people stop mistyping after about two weeks.

rules.description: D: tap types D, hold is Command
F: tap types F, hold is Shift
J: tap types J, hold is Shift
K: tap types K, hold is Command

templates.name: Home row mods: Command, Option, Control, Shift (GACS)
templates.why: Each finger on the home row also works as a shortcut key when you hold it: pinky is Command, then Option, Control, and the pointer finger is Shift. Same on both hands. Your hands never leave the middle row.
templates.forWho: People who use many shortcuts and want the most popular order, used by Miryoku and many guides.
changes: Tapping any of them types the letter
templates.caution: Eight keys act two ways, so it takes a couple of weeks to feel natural.

rules.description: A: tap types A, hold is Command
S: tap types S, hold is Option
D: tap types D, hold is Control
F: tap types F, hold is Shift
J: tap types J, hold is Shift
K: tap types K, hold is Control
L: tap types L, hold is Option
Semicolon: tap types ;, hold is Command

templates.name: Home row mods: Control, Option, Command, Shift (CAGS)
templates.why: Like the other home-row set, but ordered for Mac habits. Command, the key Mac people use most, goes on a stronger finger, and Control, which Mac people use least, goes on the pinky.
templates.forWho: Mac users who use Command all day and want the order the guide recommends for macOS.
changes: Tapping any of them types the letter
templates.caution: Same two-week learning curve as the other home-row set.

rules.description: A: tap types A, hold is Control
S: tap types S, hold is Option
D: tap types D, hold is Command
F: tap types F, hold is Shift
J: tap types J, hold is Shift
K: tap types K, hold is Command
L: tap types L, hold is Option
Semicolon: tap types ;, hold is Control

templates.name: Hold Space for arrow keys (H J K L)
templates.why: Hold the Space bar and your right hand becomes arrow keys: H is left, J is down, K is up, L is right. You can move around text without reaching for the small arrow keys. Tapping Space still types a space.
templates.forWho: Writers, coders and Vim fans who want to edit text without moving their hands.
changes: Hold Space, press H: Left Arrow
Hold Space, press J: Down Arrow
Hold Space, press K: Up Arrow
Hold Space, press L: Right Arrow
Add Command or Shift to jump or select as usual
templates.caution: Pause a tiny bit after Space when you type fast, or it may think you held it.

rules.description: Space: tap is Space, hold turns on arrow keys
H is Left Arrow
J is Down Arrow
K is Up Arrow
L is Right Arrow

templates.name: Easy-reach combos: Enter, Backspace, Escape
templates.why: Press two letter keys at the same moment to get a key that is far away. K and L together is Enter, I and O together is Backspace, W and E together is Escape. They are right under your fingers.
templates.forWho: Anyone tired of reaching for Return, Delete and Escape.
changes: Typing those letters one after the other works as usual
templates.caution: The two keys must land within about 50 thousandths of a second. If a word like "we" ever turns into Escape, you are pressing too evenly; type it a little more one-by-one.

rules.description: K and L together are Enter
I and O together are Backspace
W and E together are Escape

templates.name: Number pad under your right hand
templates.why: Hold Caps Lock and the keys under your right hand turn into a number pad, laid out like a calculator. You type numbers without reaching to the top row.
templates.forWho: People who type lots of numbers: spreadsheets, prices, codes.
changes: Hold Caps Lock: numbers on the right hand
templates.caution: This uses Caps Lock, so it cannot be combined with the Caps Lock template.

templates.name: Symbols without Shift
templates.why: Hold the right Option key and the keys under your left hand type symbols like & * ( ) $ % ^ ! @ #. No Shift needed, so shortcuts with symbols are easier.
templates.forWho: Coders and anyone who types many symbols.
changes: Hold Right Option: symbols on the left hand
Right Option does nothing else while this is on
templates.caution: Right Option stops working as Option, so skip this if you use it.

leftOut.name: Hyper key on Caps Lock
leftOut.reason: The engine can hold one modifier per key, not all four at once. Needs KE-40.

leftOut.name: One-shot Shift (tap Shift, then the next letter is capital)
leftOut.reason: The engine has no one-shot or sticky behaviour.

leftOut.name: Shift tap types ( and )
leftOut.reason: A tap action cannot carry its own Shift, so this would need engine work.

leftOut.name: Globe/Fn and Touch ID key setups
leftOut.reason: Fn and vendor keys are not visible to the engine.
